items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we are given an equation containing an exponential function, such as
[MATH: e^{t}= 12.]

Content:
We can solve it in the same way that we usually solve exponential equations, by taking the log on both sides where the base of the logarithm is the base of the exponential.

Content:
Here, the base of the exponential is [MATH: e,] so we take the natural logarithm of both sides, since
[MATH: \log_e{x} = \ln{x}.]

Content:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides, we have that
[MATH: e^{t}|= 12; \ln (e^{t})|= \ln (12).]

Content:
Now, we use the fact that [MATH: \ln \left( e^a \right) = a] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives
[MATH: t = \ln (12).]

Content:
This is the solution! We often present the solution of an exponential equation as an exact solution in logarithmic form.

items.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

sections.normalized_html: What is the value of [MATH: x] if [MATH: e^{x - 3}=2^5?]
sections.readable_text: What is the value of [MATH: x] if [MATH: e^{x - 3}=2^5?]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we take the natural logarithm [MATH: \left(\ln\right)] of both sides of the equation:

[MATH: e^{x − 3}|= 2^{5}; \ln (e^{x − 3})|= \ln (2^{5})]

Now, we use the fact that [MATH: \ln \left( e^a \right) = a] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

[MATH: x-3 = \ln \left( 2^5 \right).] Finally, we solve for [MATH: x] and rewrite the right-hand side using the power law of logarithms, as follows:

[MATH: x − 3|= \ln (2^{5}); x|= \ln (2^{5}) + 3; x|= 5\ln (2) + 3]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x=5\ln (2) + 3.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose we are given an equation containing an exponential function, such as
[MATH: e^{t}= 12.]

Content:
We can solve it in the same way that we usually solve exponential equations, by taking the log on both sides where the base of the logarithm is the base of the exponential.

Content:
Here, the base of the exponential is [MATH: e,] so we take the natural logarithm of both sides, since
[MATH: \log_e{x} = \ln{x}.]

Content:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides, we have that
[MATH: e^{t}|= 12; \ln (e^{t})|= \ln (12).]

Content:
Now, we use the fact that [MATH: \ln \left( e^a \right) = a] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives
[MATH: t = \ln (12).]

Content:
This is the solution! We often present the solution of an exponential equation as an exact solution in logarithmic form.

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

Example Prompt:
What is the value of [MATH: x] if [MATH: e^{x - 3}=2^5?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm [MATH: \left(\ln\right)] of both sides of the equation:

[MATH: e^{x − 3}|= 2^{5}; \ln (e^{x − 3})|= \ln (2^{5})]

Now, we use the fact that [MATH: \ln \left( e^a \right) = a] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

[MATH: x-3 = \ln \left( 2^5 \right).]
Finally, we solve for [MATH: x] and rewrite the right-hand side using the power law of logarithms, as follows:

[MATH: x − 3|= \ln (2^{5}); x|= \ln (2^{5}) + 3; x|= 5\ln (2) + 3]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x=5\ln (2) + 3.]

[MATH: e^{2 − 4x}|= 2; \ln (e^{2 − 4x})|= \ln (2); 2 − 4x|= \ln (2); − 4x|= \ln (2) − 2; x|= (1)/(2) − (\ln (2))/(4)]

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives
